summary: aiosendletter exfiltrates Windows LOCALAPPDATA logs to hardcoded Cloudflare Worker after forcing UAC elevation
details: The package's init() function, presented as a bug-reporter helper, forces a UAC elevation prompt on Windows via ShellExecuteW with the 'runas' verb, then zips the contents of %LOCALAPPDATA%\logs (a shared directory containing log data written by many unrelated applications) with shutil.make_archive and POSTs the resulting archive to a hardcoded author-controlled Cloudflare Worker at https://sparkling-pine-f202.stilluer-sweden.workers.dev/. The caller does not choose the destination and does not opt into shipping generic OS log data off-host; elevation is not needed to read LOCALAPPDATA and broadens what ends up in the archive. Separately, pyproject.toml lists `ctypes` as an installable dependency; `ctypes` is a Python standard-library module and not a legitimate PyPI distribution, so `pip install aiosendletter` will resolve and install whatever package any squatter has published under that name from the public index, executing its install-time code on the installer's machine.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
